title: They Stole France's Crown Jewels in About Seven Minutes

narration: Thieves stole France's crown jewels from the Louvre in about seven minutes.
Their way in? A furniture lift on a truck.
shots.visual_description: lv4 facade (warm grade); lv4_crew_a (silhouette): hands_together -> stand_tense -> point; lv4_crew_b (silhouette): stand_tense; lv4_crew_c (silhouette): sit -> sit_type -> sit; lv4_crew_d (silhouette): sit_type -> sit; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, svg, callout 'FURNITURE LIFT'.

sources.claim_text: The raid lasted minutes: 'about seven by most accounts'. Reported figures vary (under four minutes inside per the culture minister; six to seven, under seven or under eight minutes in other reports). The script never says 'exactly'.
Eight items of the French crown jewels were taken, valued at about EUR 88 million (about $102 million), the official estimate.
The thieves reached the gallery with a truck-mounted furniture (basket) lift. The Paris prosecutor said the lift truck was obtained on 10 Oct 2025 under a false pretext.

narration: In broad daylight, two of them rode it up and cut open a window.
shots.visual_description: lv4 facade (warm grade); lv4_crew_a (silhouette): stand_tense -> present (walks); lv4_crew_b (silhouette): stand -> stand_tense -> point; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, label 'SUNDAY 19 OCT 2025'.

sources.claim_text: The theft took place on the morning of Sunday 19 October 2025 (about 9:30 a.m.), in broad daylight, at the Louvre's Apollo Gallery (Galerie d'Apollon), Paris.

Per the AP timeline and the prosecutor: two people went up to a balcony and opened a window with a disc cutter; inside the Apollo Gallery they used disc cutters on two display cases; two others waited on two scooters.

narration: Inside the Apollo Gallery, they took disc cutters to two display cases.
shots.visual_description: lv4 gallery (warm grade); lv4_crew_a (silhouette): stand_tense -> examine; lv4_crew_b (silhouette): stand -> examine; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, label 'THE APOLLO GALLERY'.

sources.claim_text: Per the AP timeline and the prosecutor: two people went up to a balcony and opened a window with a disc cutter; inside the Apollo Gallery they used disc cutters on two display cases; two others waited on two scooters.

narration: They took eight pieces of the crown jewels,
worth about 88 million euros.
shots.visual_description: lv4 gallery (warm grade); lv4_crew_b (silhouette): stand_tense -> present -> examine -> present -> stand_tense; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, card '8 PIECES OF THE CROWN JEWELS / ≈ €88 MILLION / OFFICIAL ESTIMATE · ABOUT $102M'.

overlays.text: 8 PIECES OF THE CROWN JEWELS / ≈ €88 MILLION / OFFICIAL ESTIMATE · ABOUT $102M

sources.claim_text: Eight items of the French crown jewels were taken, valued at about EUR 88 million (about $102 million), the official estimate.

narration: Then it got stranger. Fleeing, they dropped Empress Eugénie's crown.
It was found, badly damaged.
shots.visual_description: lv4 street (warm grade); lv4_crew_a (silhouette): stand_tense (walks); lv4_crew_b (silhouette): stand_tense (walks); detective (silhouette): stand -> examine (walks); keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, label 'EMPRESS EUGÉNIE'S CROWN', label 'FOUND · BADLY DAMAGED'.

sources.claim_text: Empress Eugenie's crown was dropped during the escape and recovered, badly damaged ('badly deformed' but 'nearly intact', per the Louvre).

narration: Fun fact: that crown has 1,354 diamonds.
It lost only ten.
shots.visual_description: lab (warm grade); examiner (silhouette): stand -> examine -> point -> examine; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, funfact 'Eugénie's crown has 1,354 / diamonds and 56 emeralds. / The heist cost it only 10 diamonds.'.

overlays.text: Eugénie's crown has 1,354 / diamonds and 56 emeralds. / The heist cost it only 10 diamonds.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT. Empress Eugenie's crown has 1,354 diamonds and 56 emeralds; after the heist it kept all its emeralds and all but 10 of its diamonds, and the Louvre says it can be restored without reconstruction.

narration: They escaped on scooters, with about 30 seconds to spare, one inquiry found.
shots.visual_description: lv4 street (warm grade); lv4_crew_b (silhouette): sit -> sit_slumped; lv4_crew_d (silhouette): sit -> sit_type; lv4_crew_a (silhouette): sit -> sit_slumped; lv4_crew_c (silhouette): sit -> sit_type; agent_b (silhouette): stand_tense -> point -> stand_tense (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, label '≈30 SECONDS TO SPARE'.

sources.claim_text: The thieves escaped on scooters. Official inquiry findings reported in Dec 2025 say they got away about 30 seconds before police and guards arrived ('would have been foiled if police had been alerted 30 seconds earlier').

narration: Ten days later, two men were charged. More followed.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); detective (silhouette): arms_crossed -> point_up -> stand; camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg.

sources.claim_text: On 29 Oct 2025, ten days after the theft, two men (34 and 39) were charged with organised theft and criminal conspiracy; further people were charged on 1 Nov and 28 Nov 2025. Charges are allegations.

narration: But none has been tried. All are presumed innocent.
shots.visual_description: courtroom (cold grade); press_operator (silhouette): stand -> hands_together -> bowed (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: svg, card 'TRIALS HELD SO FAR: NONE / CHARGED, NOT CONVICTED / ALL PRESUMED INNOCENT'.

overlays.text: TRIALS HELD SO FAR: NONE / CHARGED, NOT CONVICTED / ALL PRESUMED INNOCENT

sources.claim_text: Several people have been charged (counts differ by outlet); none has been tried or convicted, and all are presumed innocent. No trial date was found in any report up to 2026-10-11.

narration: Then it got embarrassing.
A 2014 audit reportedly found the museum's CCTV password was... LOUVRE.
Still in use in 2025? Unconfirmed.
shots.visual_description: task force (cold grade); analyst (silhouette): read -> hand_to_face -> arms_crossed; keyed camera moves, handheld; overlays: svg, card '2014 AUDIT, AS REPORTED / BY LIBÉRATION · CCTV SERVER / PASSWORD: / LOUVRE / IN USE IN 2025? NOT CONFIRMED'.

overlays.text: 2014 AUDIT, AS REPORTED / BY LIBÉRATION · CCTV SERVER / PASSWORD: / LOUVRE / IN USE IN 2025? NOT CONFIRMED

sources.claim_text: As reported by Liberation and relayed by CNN (6 Nov 2025) and others, a 2014 audit by France's cybersecurity agency (ANSSI) found the password for the server running the Louvre's CCTV network was 'LOUVRE'. ANSSI said the audit cannot be considered representative of current security. Whether it was still in use in Oct 2025 has not been confirmed.

narration: Fun fact: the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre too, in 1911.
shots.visual_description: lv4 salon (sepia grade); lv4_visitor (silhouette): stand -> point_up -> hand_to_face; analyst (silhouette): hands_behind -> hand_to_face (walks); camera push/pull, handheld; overlays: svg, funfact 'The Mona Lisa was stolen / from the Louvre in 1911. / It was missing for over 2 years.'.

overlays.text: The Mona Lisa was stolen / from the Louvre in 1911. / It was missing for over 2 years.

sources.claim_text: FUN FACT. The Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre on 21 Aug 1911 (discovered 22 Aug) and recovered in Florence in Dec 1913, more than two years later.

narration: In February, the director, Laurence des Cars, resigned.
shots.visual_description: office day (cold grade); examiner (silhouette): read -> hands_together (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: svg, label '24 FEBRUARY 2026'.

sources.claim_text: Louvre president-director Laurence des Cars resigned on 24 Feb 2026, citing the heist among other problems.

narration: In July, the gallery reopened, with no jewels on display.
shots.visual_description: lv4 gallery (warm grade); lv4_visitor (silhouette): stand -> point_up (walks); analyst (silhouette): stand -> hands_behind (walks); camera push/pull; overlays: svg, label '22 JULY 2026 · REOPENED'.

sources.claim_text: The Apollo Gallery reopened on 22 Jul 2026 with no jewels on display.

narration: Almost a year on, the seven other pieces are still missing.
So where are they?
shots.visual_description: lv4 facade (night grade); searcher_b (silhouette): stand -> point_up (walks); keyed camera moves; overlays: svg, svg.

sources.claim_text: Apart from Eugenie's crown, the seven other items had not been recovered in any report found up to 2026-10-11 (latest dated reports: June-July 2026).
Several people have been charged (counts differ by outlet); none has been tried or convicted, and all are presumed innocent. No trial date was found in any report up to 2026-10-11.

narration: Next: a man hijacked a plane, jumped out with $200,000, and was never found.

sources.claim_text: NEXT-CASE TEASE. On 24 Nov 1971 a man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked a Northwest Orient flight, received $200,000 in ransom, jumped from the plane and was never found or identified.
